paragraphs: Shemaiah, a man of Kefar Otni.

He is mentioned in Tosefta Parah ch. 10 (Zuckermandel [edition]): Rabbi Eliezer said: There was an incident involving Shemaiah, a man of Kefar Otni, who had in his hand a flask full of purification water, and he shut the door, on which hung a key impure with corpse-impurity; and he came and asked Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai, and he said to him: Shemaiah, go and sprinkle your water. Hyman says the Tosefta reading known to him has "Rabbi Eliezer ben Shemaiah," which he calls a scribal error.

notes.text: Hyman expressly names Zuckermandel’s edition and contrasts it with the reading Eliezer ben Shemaiah. The doubled טמא in the supplied impurity description is retained as a source feature.

The consulted Machon Mamre Tosefta Parah 10:2 has Eliezer ben Shemaiah in the opening, while the reply addresses Shemaiah. Hyman’s contrasting Zuckermandel reading is reported without direct inspection of that edition.
